**Repaired finding submitted: compliant / no issue (AUDIT), confidence 0.82. Prior redline withdrawn.**

What changed and why:

- **Scope re-check.** I confirmed there is no usage, metering or licence-compliance audit right binding us anywhere in the agreement — no audit/inspect/verify/examine/records-access language against Customer; § 4.1–4.2 have IBM meter and invoice its own usage Charges with no right to audit our books; § 12.1 grants the Base Components licence with no compliance-verification right.
- **§ 11.3 is out of scope.** It is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating suspected breaches of the content warranties in § 11.2(b)), i.e. a security and illegal-content mechanism, not the metering audit AUDIT targets.
- **Why the earlier graft was wrong.** It would have collided with p0137's emergency/required-by-law carve-out, capped IBM at one investigation a year even for a second security or abuse incident, imported an inoperative 5% underpayment trigger where nothing is measured, and cut across p0138 and IBM's remedies in 11.3(a)/(b) in a hosting deal where IBM runs the environment.
- **Direction.** The absence of any audit right against us is better than the playbook preferred position, so no redline was proposed. Flagged for follow-up: apply the AUDIT parameters if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification.
